grandparents_cupboard.reason: Fruit, oats, flour, almonds, sugar, oil and cinnamon are all plain cupboard and garden staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Seedless grapes, blackberries and everything else are everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, a bowl and fingertip rubbing, which any beginner can manage.

works.reason: 600g of fruit under a 75g oat, 75g flour and 4 tbsp oil crumble at 190°C for 25 to 30 minutes gives a sensible crumble for four, with cornflour to thicken the juices.

honest_times.reason: Halving 400g grapes, chopping a few almonds and rubbing in fit within 15 minutes, and 30 minutes baking plus 10 minutes cooling matches the 40 minutes of cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, red seedless grapes are honestly grapes, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Grapes are the main fruit at 400g, with early August blackberries in support, and a warm crumble suits the date.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is mostly fruit with oats, wholemeal flour and almonds and only 40g sugar for four, so it makes a real snack the family would want again.
